title: A shared debris-return delay can preserve the ASASSN-14ko X-ray clock under steady orbital decay
abstract: We test whether a stable X-ray to UV lag proves a stable stellar orbit in ASASSN-14ko. For five published Swift XRT ingress times, an exact constant period derivative of -0.0026 admits a common delay range of 1.4571 days when epoch and period are free and errors are bounded by twice the reported error with a 0.5-day floor in quadrature. A three-event contrast proves this sharp bound. An ideal constant event period over 13 cycles needs a 5.9558-day delay range. We derive a positive, mass-preserving change of debris energy density that translates a ballistic return pulse by this amount without changing its width or internal lags. A synthetic example passes a necessary tidal-energy support check. This is a proof of ambiguity under stated assumptions, not a physical model of the star or evidence for steady orbital decay. Stellar structure, relativity, and full energy conservation remain untested. Fixed inter-band lags and rejection of a uniform fallback stretch do not alone establish an orbital stall.

display.caption: Sharp X-ray delay bounds, an exact synthetic return-pulse translation, and necessary tidal-energy support limits under stated assumptions.
